The mead hall

Eight meads, eight stories.

Every one is honey fermented with Pacific Northwest fruit, then named for someone out of the old stories. Tap a bottle to read who.

Our sweetest offering — a luscious sweet mead crafted entirely from Pacific Northwest ingredients. Named for the mythical goat of Valhalla whose udder flowed with endless mead, this pour is rich, golden, and made to be savored.

750 ml · 14% ABV

Our traditional dry mead — clean, crisp and unsweetened. Named for the great stag of Valhalla whose antlers feed the rivers of the world, it lets the character of the honey shine through with nothing added.

750 ml · 14% alcohol

Bright, fruit-forward and made with blueberries. Named for the healing giantess of Lyfjaberg, this pour brings honey and ripe northwest berries together into something as vibrant as it is smooth.

750 ml · 14% by volume

Bold, tart and made with raspberries. Named for Angrboda, the giantess who birthed Fenrir, Jörmungandr and Hel — as fierce as she is, and as beautiful.

750 ml · 14% strength

Crisp, smooth and full of orchard character. Named for the ancient giant whose knowledge rivalled Odin's own, it puts honey and northwest apples in the same glass — as thoughtful as it is refreshing.

750 ml · 14% abv

Dark, bold and made with blackberries. Named for the goddess who rules the realm of the dead, it comes out deep and brooding — the label has her on her throne between two wolves.

750 ml · 14%

A sweet mead aged in barrels for one to two years. Named for the fire giant who guards Muspelheim and carries the flames of Ragnarök — honeyed sweetness deepened by time and oak.

750 ml · 14% alc by vol

Rich, tart and made with cherries. Named for the giant who guarded the Mead of Poetry itself — a jewel-red pour worthy of the legend it's named after.

750 ml · 14 percent

The tap room

Where the mead ends up.

Everything in the bottle starts close to home — the honey, the fruit, the water. It doesn't travel far to reach the glass.

Tastings by appointment

Call ahead and sit down with us in the tap room. Tuesday through Saturday, by appointment — so the door is open when you get here.

Bottles to carry out

750 ml, corked and sealed, ready to take with you.

Shipped out of Buckley

We ship nationwide, or you can pick up right here in Buckley. Two bottles is the smallest order that fits in a box.

Found around town

Beyond the tap room, a few places around the plateau carry it. Give us a ring and we’ll tell you who has it on the shelf right now.

Where it comes from

Made in Buckley, named in Jötunheim.

Jötunheim is the giants' realm in the Norse stories — and every mead on the list is named for somebody who lives there.

The honey, the berries and the water all come from around here. Blueberries, raspberries, blackberries, cherries and apples get and go straight in with the honey, and then it's a matter of waiting. The barrel-aged one waits one to two years.

It's fermented and bottled in town under Winkelhaus Enterprises, and every label is drawn by hand: a knotwork border wrapped around a scene from whichever story the mead is named after. Hel on her throne between two wolves.

Out of the cellar

Corked, sealed and carried to the fire.

    Taste from dry to sweet, take home whatever you liked best.
